architecture: ARCH2 — generate the surfaces instead of condensing them (campaign programs C4 + C5)
question_asked: How much of this code should be written by hand at all?
distinct_from_attempt_1: Attempt 1 asked what could be removed from existing code and hit floors. This asked whether whole families of handwritten code could be replaced by output from a single reviewed authority -- a different mechanism, not a different effort level.
why: The handwritten mirror surface across the owned paths is roughly 98 lines. The C4/C5 generative machinery already exists in crates/hawking-adapters and hide-sdk, and has already replaced the large command, protocol, adapter, CLI-surface and SDK mirrors. What remains in those paths is sole-authority definition, actual behaviour, or the dual event surfaces marked must_not_delete until the Bridge lane. A new generator cannot eliminate 25,000 lines that are not handwritten restatements of anything.
significance: This is the campaign's second structural mechanism and it is refuted on measurement rather than on effort. The repository has already absorbed the generative architecture; there is no second helping of it available.
lane_behaviour: Correct. It measured the mirror surface before building anything and stopped when the number came back at 0.39% of target, rather than constructing a generator that would have saved nothing and cost lines.
